newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Restructuring BTR profits seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Restructuring BTR profits seen down.

text.p: Anglo-Australian industrial conglomerate BTR Plc, in the midst of an ambitious shake-up, is expected to report lower profits on Thursday when analysts will be keenly awaiting latest details of the group's revival drive.
"We are looking for more progress on restructuring and whether they have identified more disposal candidates," said Zafar Khan at SocGen.
BTR, which has 1,000 businesses across the world, is expected to report 1996 pretax profit of between 728 million and 1.25 billion stg.
The company, which has already completed two thirds of its planned divestments, posted a pre-tax profit of 1.503 billion stg for 1995.
Following recent disposals, BTR said in December it planned to compare its 1996 performance with pro-rata 1995 sales of 7.7 billion stg and operating profits of about 1.4 billion stg.
Chief executive Ian Strachan, brought in early last year to streamline BTR, set out a drastic action plan in September to address the company's cash flow problems.
BTR aims to achieve further growth by focusing on its top industrial manufacturing and engineering operations and wield out underperforming activities.

The company warned late last year that the strong pound would have some negative impact, but cheered investors as it forecast that its trading performance in the second half of the year would be better than in the first.
